overview.text: Prince Hamlet of Denmark is the central character in Shakespeare’s revenge tragedy. After his father dies and his uncle Claudius becomes king, a ghost claiming to be Hamlet’s father accuses Claudius of murder and calls for revenge. Hamlet tries to test the accusation by arranging a play that echoes the alleged killing and watching Claudius’s response. His behavior appears mad to other characters, while the play leaves open whether he is pretending, truly distressed, or both. Hamlet is also known for soliloquies that wrestle with life, death, and action; his uncertainty and delay make him more complicated than a straightforward avenger.

key_facts.text: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark and the son of the late King Hamlet; Claudius, his uncle, becomes king and marries Hamlet’s mother, Gertrude.
The Ghost claims Claudius murdered Hamlet’s father and demands revenge; the play presents this as the Ghost’s allegation to Hamlet.
Hamlet uses a traveling actors’ performance of a murder resembling the Ghost’s account to observe Claudius’s reaction and test his guilt.
Whether Hamlet is truly mad or only pretending is one of the play’s unresolved questions.
The famous “To be or not to be” soliloquy reflects the play’s attention to life, death, and Hamlet’s struggle over what to do.
